title: What if you became a millionaire at sixteen?
fact_source: UTMA custodial accounts: custodian controls assets until termination age, usually 18 or 21 depending on state (Motley Fool 'UTMA'; finaid.org age of majority; Nolo/WillMaker UTMA). Compound growth: 1,000,000 × 1.07^49 ≈ 27.5 million (simple arithmetic, assumes 7 % average annual return, not guaranteed).

lines.text: What if you became a millionaire at sixteen?
It's a boring Monday. You're sixteen, walking home from school, with eleven dollars in your account.
Then your phone buzzes. A deposit. One million dollars. In your name.
You refresh the app three times. It's still there.
But in the US, money for a minor usually sits in a custodial account. An adult controls it, not you, until you turn eighteen.
So you tell one friend. Just one.
By dinner, your whole school knows. Two hundred new followers. Forty messages from people you've never talked to.
Your cousin needs a loan. Your uncle has a business idea.
Invested at seven percent a year, that million could be over twenty five million when you retire.
Or you ignore all of that, and buy the car anyway. Because you're sixteen.
You post one picture with it. Two million views by the morning.
Then, at midnight, your phone buzzes again.
Bank error. Funds reversed. Eleven dollars.
Be honest. What would you have bought first?
